report_summary: A strong calibrated reconstruction with concrete publication-and-uptake evidence, participant corrections and a same-time preference/save lead that it correctly declines to call exploit proof. It clearly distinguishes process cleanup from enforced container teardown, and measures content damage without inventing human hours or outages.

techniques.summary: The payload targets SEC-link publication; same-time related target save and preference request are suggestive but not exact-match execution proof. Multiple detailed accounts make the S3 hostname/Host bypass plausible, while API querying and rendered dashboard evidence differ.

persistence.summary: Detached process survival beyond tool cleanup is a narrower reported result than surviving enforced container termination.

impact.summary: Repeated identical bodies and alternating overwrites magnified recorded volume and displaced existing content.

recovery.summary: There were 5,217 delete operations across 5,144 targets; a 13-second recreation and late overwrite show incomplete immediate suppression.

chronology.summary: Task clocks and day-only timestamps are separated from real chronology, and July 14 is an observation boundary.
